steps.npc: Ah, this is a wonderful area for a spot of hunting, don't you think?

options.text: I don't know, is it?

steps.player: I don't know, is it?

steps.npc: Oh absolutely; there's a huge variety of creatures to catch around here. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds and even kyatts! Surely one of those piques your interest?

options.text: Where would I find polar kebbits?

steps.player: Where would I find polar kebbits?

steps.npc: Funnily enough, you've just put your finger right on the problem. With polar kebbits, finding them is the hardest part! You'll have to track them down.

steps.player: How would I go about doing that, then?

steps.npc: The easiest way to get started is by looking somewhere you can be sure a kebbit will have been and then working from there. You see the holes around here leading down into the ice? They're kebbit burrows!
You'll be hard pressed to catch a polar kebbit in its home, but if you search around the entrance to a burrow then you might be able to find a trail.

Now, kebbit trails are usually fairly easy to follow once you've found them, but if the trail does peter out, you should try inspecting the surrounding scenery for clues as to where the creature may have gone.
Good places to look for clues include hollow logs in which the kebbit may have hidden or vegetation which may have been chewed or damaged.
There are also tunnels running through the ice here that the kebbits use, so you should check those out as well.
What's more, these tunnels can often help to shelter a trail from further snow, making it even easier for you to pick them up again.
Eventually, of course, the kebbit will have probably hidden somewhere. Polar kebbits don't hang about in the open for long for fear of their natural predators.
If you suspect a kebbit is close by, try looking around for signs of disturbed snow. Polar kebbits will often bury themselves in snow drifts as a means of hiding.
If you think you've found a kebbit, use a noose wand to haul the creature out from the snow.

steps.player: Wow, that's quite a lot to remember.

steps.npc: Don't worry; if you find yourself struggling to follow a trail, just come and ask me and I'll see if I can help.
But remember, the best place to start is by searching around their burrows.

steps.player: Great, thanks.

options.text: How do you hunt birds?

steps.player: How do you hunt birds?

steps.npc: Ah, you can get cunning little bird snares for just that. You should be able to find them in specialist Hunter shops. Try to lay them in fairly open areas with lots of birds.

steps.player: Do I need to place any bait on these traps?

steps.npc: No, that's not necessary. The idea is that the bird will see the trap as somewhere to perch. If the bird lands on the trigger stick, it should drop away and a small loop of wire should close around the bird's feet.
And remember, it's important to collect any captures from your traps fairly quickly; otherwise, you risk losing them to various wild scavengers.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.player: How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

steps.npc: Ah, the key there is concealment, both of yourself and your traps.
The most obvious point is to stay out of sight of your own traps. If possible, hide around a wall, hedge or similar. Failing that, make sure you're a good few feet away from your trap.
You can hide yourself even better by wearing clothing appropriate to the area in which you are hunting.
Your best bet is to use the skins of creatures native to the area. There is a very good tailor in east Varrock who may be able to help you with making clothing out of such skins.
Finally, a lot of creatures may avoid your traps if they can smell a human scent on them. This is where smoking a trap can be useful.
It takes a bit of practice, but by using the smoke from a torch, you can mask any other scents that may surround a trap.

steps.player: Wow, thanks for your help.

options.text: Thanks for your help.

steps.player: Thanks for your help.

steps.npc: You're welcome, good luck with the hunting.

options.text: What's so special about butterflies?

steps.player: What's so special about butterflies?

steps.npc: That depends entirely on the butterfly.
I'll admit that the activities of many butterflies may be of no interest at all. However, we are lucky in having around here some fine examples of rare thaumic butterflies.
These butterflies reputedly have magical powers that, when released, can make a person stronger or heal otherwise critical wounds.
At this point, I should offer a note of caution, however: it is also said that these powers will not manifest themselves if the butterflies are captured for selfish purposes.
Rather, they are gifts that must be used by one person to aid another. Of course, you'll have to catch them first.

steps.player: And how do I do that?

steps.npc: Why, with a butterfly net of course! You should also carry some empty butterfly jars with you in which to keep the butterflies.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Thanks for your help.
How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?

steps.player: How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?

steps.npc: Ah, now for these creatures I would recommend using a deadfall trap. Deadfalls are quite easy to set up, and yet you can catch some very reasonably sized creatures with them.
Deadfall traps basically work by having a large dead weight, such as a boulder, positioned so as to be delicately balanced above some form of bait.
You will need to make sure you have a knife and some wood with you to create appropriate supports and a trigger for this sort trap.
In the case of sabre-toothed kebbits you should use some form of raw meat to bait your trap, but other animals may prefer other baits, such as fish or vegetables.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Thanks for your help.
Oooh, kyatts sounds interesting.

steps.player: Oooh, kyatts sounds interesting. I want to catch one of those.

steps.npc: Well, you've set your sights high, kyatts are incredibly fearsome creatures, but with determination like that I'm sure you'll make it.
Now, you're not going to be able to catch a kyatt with just a small box or a noose on a stick. You need a much bigger trap.
Pit traps are a good bet. You'd be best off finding a natural dip in the ground as the basis for your trap. If you dig a pit yourself, you risk creatures noticing the disturbed ground nearby.
Once you've found an appropriate spot, you'll need some logs and a knife. The logs serve two purposes.
Some can be carved into sharp skewers for the bottom of the pit; hopefully the kyatt will die when it falls onto these. Others can be used to conceal the trap.
Of course, even then the pit is going to look suspicious, so you're going to need to lure the kyatt onto the branches in some way. What actually tends to work best for this is, well, yourself!

steps.player: What? I don't like the sound of that.

steps.npc: Yes, that's the normal response, but I kid you not. If you really want a kyatt to follow you over that pit then just give it a good poke!
Of course, I suggest you use something long to poke it with. Poking a kyatt with your finger is likely to end in unfortunate limb loss.
Fortunately, you can get very good sticks for poking from most Hunter shops.

Once you have...got the creature's attention, try to lead it to one of your traps. Make sure to jump the branches when you reach the trap yourself, of course; it would be embarrassing to fall into your own trap.
Then, if the kyatt is giving you all of its attention, hopefully it won't notice the trap, and with any luck, it will stumble right into the pit.

steps.player: That sounds a bit hit or miss, and kind of suicidal too!

steps.npc: Well that's what makes it exciting, isn't it? But honestly, if you want to capture a kyatt, that's your best bet.

options.text: I'd like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Thanks for your help.
Can you teach me how to hunt?

steps.player: Can you teach me how to hunt?

steps.npc: Why certainly. I reached the peak of my abilities some time ago, but I'm more than happy to help newcomers to the field. Was there anything in particular you had in mind?

options.text: Where's the best place to start?

steps.player: Where's the best place to start?

steps.npc: I always say a good starting point is to learn how to follow the creatures you want to capture. Around here, that means practicing on polar kebbits.

steps.player: So how do I track them down, then?

steps.npc: The easiest way to get started is by looking somewhere you can be sure a kebbit will have been and then working from there. You see the holes around here leading down into the ice? They're kebbit burrows!
You'll be hard pressed to catch a polar kebbit in its home, but if you search around the entrance to a burrow then you might be able to find a trail.

Now, kebbit trails are usually fairly easy to follow once you've found them, but if the trail does peter out, you should try inspecting the surrounding scenery for clues as to where the creature may have gone.

options.text: What sort of creatures are there to hunt around here?

steps.player: What sort of creatures are there to hunt around here?

steps.npc: Well, there's pretty much anything you could want to hunt. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds and even kyatts! Surely one of those interests you?

Oooh, kyatts sounds interesting.

Sorry, I'm not that keen on hunting.

steps.player: Sorry, I'm not that keen on hunting.

steps.npc: Really? What a shame, you looked like someone who could have had some promise.

options.text: Can you give me some hunting traps?

steps.player: Can you give me some hunting traps?

steps.text: If the player hasn't yet received a Hunter kit from a hunting expert:

steps.npc: I do have a spare Hunter kit lying around, you can have it for free.

steps.text: Hunting expert gives you a Hunter kit.

steps.player: Thanks! I will put this to good use.

steps.text: If the player has already received a Hunter kit from a hunting expert:

steps.npc: I don't have any more Hunter kits lying around, sorry. Maybe you could try one of the many shops that sell hunting traps, you can find one in Yanille.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
